fact: The Countdown to 2030 report presented by Senegal's health ministry directorates analyses facility data reported through DHIS2 for 2019-2024, including by district and region.

The report states that the share of districts with report completeness of 90% or more was 57% in 2024 for reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health (antenatal care and delivery) in DHIS2, and gives an overall data-quality score of 63% in 2024.
Senegal's health ministry said it operates a unified national platform based on DHIS2 for health information.
The ministry said the national DHIS2 platform has been extended to epidemiological surveillance, human resources, the supply chain and maternal and perinatal death surveillance.
Since January 2025 all districts have begun entering health data on the national platform, says the ministry's health information division head.
Ministry official Tidjane Gadjaga says health data completeness rose from under 30% to 80% after unions lifted their data retention in January 2025.
